name: Teia Calendar Contract
description: On-chain registry for the Teia community calendar. Each event is identified by an auto-incrementing integer event_id and stores its current IPFS/Arweave CID and a hidden flag. Version history is not kept on-chain: every event mutation emits a version event (tag event_created or event_updated) carrying the CID, editor, optional proposer, version number and timestamp, from which an indexer reconstructs the full history without paying for an unbounded on-chain big_map. All event details (title, start/end date, location, description, links, images) live off-chain in the event's CID content. Moderators and linked multisig users can create, update and hide events directly. Teia token holders can submit proposals to edit an existing event (propose_edit) or to create a brand new event (propose_event); each proposal action charges its own configurable fee, forwarded to the fee recipient (typically the Teia multisig), and any fee can be set to 0 via governance. A moderator or multisig user approves or rejects pending proposals; a single approval applies the change (appending a new version to the event, or creating the event and assigning it the next integer id). Multisig governance covers pause, the linked multisig/moderator/token addresses, the token id, per-action fees, the fee recipient and contract metadata updates; governance proposals require a minimum number of votes and expire after a configurable time, both fetched from the linked multisig contract.
